source.board: NCCER (National Center for Construction Education and Research)

masonry.note: Units follow the NCCER masonry levels — safety and tools, mortar and materials, and the laying crafts of brick, block and stone.

lesson.title: Masonry Safety and Tools
lesson.summary: The mason's kit and its hazards — lifting discipline, trowels and jointers, and working safely at height.

lesson.title: Mortar and Masonry Materials
lesson.summary: The glue and the units — mortar types by strength, brick grades and how much to order.

lesson.title: Laying Brick and Block
lesson.summary: The core craft — bonds, the gauge rod, and joints tooled for weather.

lesson.title: Stone, Veneer and Reinforced Masonry
lesson.summary: Beyond the brick wall — natural stone setting, veneer systems and steel-reinforced masonry.

lesson.title: Weather Resistance and Quality
lesson.summary: Keeping water out — flashing, weep holes and the inspection criteria that grade masonry work.

source.board: National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology (NIC)
source.document: Official published exam content areas (scientific concepts, hair care, skin care, nails)

cosmetology.note: Units follow the NIC content areas — infection control and sciences, hair care and services, skin care, and nails.

lesson.title: Infection Control and Salon Safety
lesson.summary: The licence's first duty — disinfection levels, chemistry safety and protecting every client.

lesson.title: Hair: Structure and Services
lesson.summary: Hair as chemistry — structure, the colour wheel, perming and relaxing chemistry.

lesson.title: Skin Care Services
lesson.summary: The skin side of the licence — structure, facial treatment and safe hair removal.

lesson.title: Nail Technology
lesson.summary: Nails as structures — disorders you must recognise, natural nail care and enhancement systems.

lesson.title: Cosmetology as a Profession
lesson.summary: The licensed business — scope of practice, consultations and building a career ethically.

source.board: American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) Board of Certification

phlebotomy.note: Units follow the PBT content areas — the circulatory system, venipuncture procedure, specimen handling and the legal and professional frame.

units.title: Circulatory anatomy and physiology
topics: Vein selection and sites to avoid

lesson.title: Veins and Blood: the Phlebotomist's Map
lesson.summary: Which veins, which order, which sites never — the anatomy every safe draw depends on.

lesson.title: The Venipuncture Procedure
lesson.summary: The draw itself — order of draw, tube chemistry and why some sticks fail.

lesson.title: Specimen Handling
lesson.summary: The draw is half the job — labelling law, transport rules and what makes a specimen unusable.

lesson.title: Special Populations and POC Testing
lesson.summary: The harder draws — children, fragile veins and bedside testing accuracy.

lesson.title: Legal and Professional Standards
lesson.summary: The trust framework — ID protocols, confidentiality and the professional conduct of blood draws.

nuclear-medicine-technology.note: Units follow the NMTCB content areas — radiopharmacy, instrumentation, imaging procedures and radiation safety.

lesson.title: Radiopharmaceuticals
lesson.summary: Drugs that glow — how radioisotopes are made, attached to medicines and sent to specific organs.

lesson.title: Gamma Cameras, SPECT and PET
lesson.summary: Seeing the glow — how gamma cameras, SPECT and PET turn radiation into diagnostic images.

lesson.title: Nuclear Medicine Procedures
lesson.summary: The clinical catalogue — bone, heart, thyroid, kidney and lung studies and what each answers.

lesson.title: Safety in Nuclear Medicine
lesson.summary: Radiation with a purpose — ALARA for patients and staff, pregnancy rules and spill response.

lesson.title: Therapy and Theranostics
lesson.summary: From imaging to treatment — radioiodine, peptide therapy and the theranostics pairing of diagnosis and cure.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Mining and Similarly Named Engineering Programs

mining-engineering.note: Units follow ABET's required mining curriculum areas — exploration, mine design, extraction methods, and the safety, environment and economics of extraction.

lesson.title: Ore Deposits and Exploration
lesson.summary: Finding what's worth mining — ore formation, exploration tools and the arithmetic of reserves.

lesson.title: Surface Mining
lesson.summary: Mining from the top down — pit geometry, blasting science and the truck fleets that move mountains.

lesson.title: Underground Mining
lesson.summary: Mining from below — method selection, rock support and the ventilation that keeps miners breathing.

lesson.title: Mineral Processing
lesson.summary: From rock to concentrate — crushing, grinding, flotation and the responsible handling of tailings.

lesson.title: Safety, Environment and Economics
lesson.summary: The licence to operate — safety engineering, environmental stewardship and the economics of closure.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Ocean Engineering and Similarly Named Programs

naval-architecture.note: Units follow ABET's ocean/naval curriculum areas — hydrostatics, resistance and propulsion, structures, and the marine environment's engineering demands.

lesson.title: Floating Things Steadily: Hydrostatics
lesson.summary: Why ships float upright — buoyancy, the metacentre and the stability every hull must prove.

lesson.title: Hull Forms and Resistance
lesson.summary: Designing the shape that slips — hull geometry, drag components and the tank tests that verify them.

lesson.title: Marine Propulsion
lesson.summary: Pushing ships forward — propeller theory, cavitation's dangers and the fuels decarbonising shipping.

lesson.title: Ship Structures and Sea Loads
lesson.summary: Building for a moving ocean — wave loading, hull strength and the corrosion-fatigue marathon.

lesson.title: Offshore and Ocean Engineering
lesson.summary: Beyond the ship — platforms, subsea systems and the ocean's renewable energy engineering.

source.track: certification · music therapy board certification domains

music-therapy.note: Units follow the CBMT domains — assessment, treatment planning, implementation, documentation and the profession's foundations.

units.title: Foundations of music therapy
topics: How music affects the brain and body

lesson.title: What Music Therapy Is
lesson.summary: Music as clinical tool — the research on how rhythm and melody reach brains that speech cannot.

lesson.title: Assessment Through Music
lesson.summary: Hearing the client — how therapists assess movement, memory and emotion through musical response.

lesson.title: Designing Music-based Treatment
lesson.summary: From goal to song — choosing between singing, improvising and listening to hit clinical targets.

lesson.title: Music Therapy Across Populations
lesson.summary: Where the evidence sings — stroke rehab, autism, mental health and dementia's remarkable responses.

lesson.title: The Music Therapy Profession
lesson.summary: The accountable practice — documentation, ethics and music therapists inside clinical teams.

art-therapy.note: Units follow the ATCB content areas — the profession's history and theory, assessment through art, treatment approaches, and standards of practice.

lesson.title: What Art Therapy Is
lesson.summary: Making images as clinical work — how the field began and why the process, not the product, heals.

lesson.title: Assessing Through Art
lesson.summary: Reading process, not pictures — assessment methods, media choice and the cultural care images demand.

lesson.title: Art Therapy Treatment
lesson.summary: The working methods — directive versus open studio, trauma-informed practice and the group setting.

lesson.title: Art Therapy Across Populations
lesson.summary: Where it practises — children, hospitals, dementia care and the adaptations each demands.

lesson.title: The Art Therapy Profession
lesson.summary: The credential's duties — image confidentiality, supervision and the evidence behind the practice.

source.qualification: Triplehorn & Johnson — Borrer and DeLong's Introduction to the Study of Insects

entomology.note: Units follow the canonical structure — insect evolution and anatomy, the major orders, insect biology and ecology, and applied entomology.

lesson.title: Insects: the Dominant Animals
lesson.summary: Why insects rule Earth — the arthropod body plan, six legs and the anatomy of the most successful animals.

lesson.title: Metamorphosis: Two Ways to Grow Up
lesson.summary: Caterpillar to butterfly and its simpler cousins — the hormones and life cycles of insect growth.

lesson.title: A Tour of the Major Orders
lesson.summary: The field guide in one lesson — beetles to bees, what defines each big order and how to tell them apart.

lesson.title: Insect Ecology and Behaviour
lesson.summary: Insects running the world — coevolution with flowers, superorganism societies and food-web roles.

lesson.title: Applied Entomology
lesson.summary: Insects as pests, pollinators, disease vectors and detectives — the applied side of the six-legged world.
